create.name: Santipada Buddhist Monastery
create.bio:
Santipada, whose Pali name means a state of peace, is a small Buddhist monastery in the hills of Northland, about twenty minutes' drive from Kerikeri. It follows a blended path that draws on both Korean Zen and the Theravada tradition, and its community is made up of monks, nuns and lay followers. The abbot, Bhante Yasala, was ordained as a nun in Korea in 1984, spent four years in a silent mountain retreat and later trained in Myanmar and India before settling in New Zealand in 2003. Bhante Anuttara, a Korean-born monk who ordained in 2008 and moved to New Zealand in 2015, teaches alongside her.

Every Sunday morning the monastery opens for walking and sitting practice and a Dhamma talk, with a short beginners' class beforehand, and all teaching is given on a donation basis. Visitors may stay as paying retreatants for three nights or more, join a seven-day retreat that starts on the last Sunday of each month, or live in as volunteers who share the daily timetable of chanting, meditation and work. A monthly membership scheme includes an annual retreat, and Bhante Anuttara's written reflections are posted on the site.

courses.title: 7 Day Meditation Retreat
courses.description: A week inside the monastery's own routine, beginning on the final Sunday of every month. Retreatants join the shared morning and evening chanting and sitting, about three hours a day, and can ask for extra sessions that bring the total to around seven hours.

courses.title: General Retreat
courses.description: A personal retreat of three nights or longer, shaped with one of the monastic teachers around the daily timetable of chanting, group sittings and a midday Dhamma discussion. Guests keep the monastery's precepts during their stay.
courses.price: $150NZ per day – general retreat ( minimum 3 nights)

courses.title: Membership Retreats
courses.description: Supporters who give monthly through a calendar year receive the newsletter, guidance from the teachers and an annual retreat whose length grows with the level chosen, from three days up to ten or more.
courses.price: Dhamma Rain – $30 per month; Dhamma Stream – $50 per month; Dhamma River – $80 per month; Dhamma Ocean & Beyond – $100 per month or more

courses.title: Volunteer stays
courses.description: Volunteers live at the monastery and follow a timetable of chanting, group sittings, Dhamma discussion and working meditation, treating giving, conduct and meditation as one practice. Food, lodging and guidance are offered without charge.

free_resources.title: Sunday Meditation
free_resources.description: An open Sunday morning of walking and sitting meditation followed by a Dhamma talk, with a half-hour instruction class for newcomers beforehand. Offered on a donation basis.

free_resources.title: Dhamma Reflections
free_resources.description: Short written teachings by Bhante Anuttara, posted as downloadable newsletters, on themes such as walking meditation, right concentration, right effort and right intention.
